Chapter 9: Living with Uncertainty
If there’s one thing therapy really teaches us, it’s this: life is just full of uncertainty. No matter how carefully you plan, or how much you prepare, there’s always something you just can’t predict.
And let’s be honest, that can be pretty unsettling, right? For a lot of us, it’s a source of anxiety—like the ground could shift beneath us at any moment.
Even therapists aren’t immune to these feelings. Imagine a therapist, still reeling from her own sudden loss, wrestling with the same truth she helps others face. She wanted guarantees—some kind of assurance that things would turn out okay. But her therapist gently reminded her: certainty is really just an illusion. The real challenge? Learning to live with not knowing.
Think about one client who came in, facing a tough medical diagnosis with no clear outcome. She did what so many of us do—she scoured the internet for answers, searched for second opinions, tried every remedy she could find. But in therapy, she started to notice the toll all this searching was taking on her mind and body.
Gradually, she practiced letting go. She focused on what she could actually control, and tried to make space for what she couldn’t.
Then there was another client, anxious about where his marriage was heading. He really wanted a roadmap—a checklist that would guarantee success. But, just like life, relationships are unpredictable.
In therapy, he learned to sit with ambiguity, to stay present even when things felt shaky. And here’s what he discovered—trust isn’t about knowing exactly how things will turn out. It’s about showing up with honesty and openness, even when the future’s unclear.
The therapist herself found she was practicing these same lessons, right alongside her clients. She learned to sit with discomfort, and to resist that urge to rush in and fix everything.
What she discovered? Uncertainty may be uncomfortable, but it’s also a space where new possibilities can emerge—a place where something unexpected and beautiful might just take root.
